guide.title: How AsBeez works
guide.heroLead: AsBeez is a community marketplace where shopping is designed to become lasting participation — not a one-time checkout.
guide.heroCopy: This page explains the designed business model: members, partners, Reward Points (RP), AsBeez Business Cells (ABC), and the Beehive Matrix. Use it to understand the Hive before you join.
guide.designNotice: The marketplace catalog is live. Reward Points (RP), Business Cells (ABC), Hive Credits (AHC), wallets, and withdrawals are the designed rewards model. They are not available to spend or cash out on this site yet. Figures below are default examples from the business design and can change by country.
guide.glanceTitle: The whole path, in one look
guide.glanceCaption: Read the page for the rules. This strip is the picture: shopping creates points, points create Cells, Cells sit in a 3-by-12, and Hive Credits stay Hive Credits until you ask to convert them.
guide.lifeMatrixCopy: The Cell takes the next open seat.
guide.lifeConvertCopy: Dollars only after you request it.
guide.unitRpCopy: Born from the partner's agreed Platform Participation Fee (PPF). They stack toward a Cell. They are not the price you paid, and they are not cash.
guide.unitAbcCopy: A permanent seat in that country's Matrix. You can own many. Each one looks down its own 3-by-12.
guide.unitAhcCopy: The earning unit of a Cell. They stay AHC in the wallet until you request conversion to dollars.
guide.benefitMemberCopy: A free account, a catalog to buy from, Reward Points from Platform Participation Fees, and as many Business Cells as your shopping creates.
guide.benefitVendorCopy: A branded storefront, members already shopping in the Hive, and a Platform Participation Fee that can fund Reward Points for buyers.
guide.placeGraphicCaption: Every new ABC — yours or someone else's — takes the next open seat. A Cell you own can sit under another Cell you also own. Each Cell still has its own 3-by-12 from that seat.
guide.placeOwnHint: Also yours, in the next open seat
guide.convertGraphicCaption: Tables on this page count AsBeez Hive Credits. The wallet holds AHC. A dollar amount appears only after you request conversion or withdrawal, and only if that request is approved.
guide.convertStayCopy: Hive Credits sit in the wallet.
guide.convertAskCopy: Nothing becomes money until you ask.
guide.convertDollarsCopy: Only after approval under financial policy.
guide.flyCaption: Each turn of the loop is meant to make the next purchase more useful. No one fills a 3-by-12 by shopping alone.
guide.flyShopCopy: Purchases create a Platform Participation Fee and Reward Points.
guide.flyVendorsCopy: Sales and a growing catalog keep sellers in the Hive.
guide.flyCellsCopy: Enough points create ABCs that take the next open seats.
guide.flyCreditsCopy: Qualified Cells may receive AHC. Loyalty brings people back.
guide.referralMeterTitle: Referrals unlock depth, they do not start the engine
guide.referralMeterCaption: Shopping can create Cells with zero referrals. Each bar is how many of the twelve floors that Cell can count.
guide.manyGraphicCaption: Each ABC is a separate 3-by-12. The ceilings on this page are for one Cell. More shopping can create more Cells, each with its own tree.
guide.whyP1: Most digital shopping ends when the payment clears. Loyalty points sit in a brand silo, referrals sit in another tool, and the relationship disappears until the next ad.
guide.whyP2: AsBeez starts from a different question: what if participation itself became valuable? Every qualified purchase is meant to strengthen the member, the partner, and the wider Hive — not only the cart total.
guide.quoteFounder: What if participation itself became valuable?
guide.whatTitle: A marketplace with a participation layer
guide.whatP1: AsBeez is not only a storefront. The design combines a multi-partner marketplace, a rewards lifecycle, an optional referral network, and shared platform tools for businesses.
guide.whatP2: Five pillars hold the model up:
guide.whatItem1: Marketplace — products and services; without commerce there is no Hive.
guide.whatItem2: Partners — businesses that sell from their own branded storefronts.
guide.whatItem3: Members — people who browse, buy, and optionally refer others.
guide.whatItem4: Technology — the rails; it serves people, it is not the product.
guide.whatItem5: The Hive — the combined strength of every participant.
guide.whatP3: Membership is free. Participation is voluntary. The long-term aim is one membership across many industries. Launch focus begins with digital listings and expands as the catalog grows.
guide.journeyP1: You do not buy a Business Cell. You shop. The partner's agreed PPF on that purchase is designed to create RP, and enough RP create a Business Cell.
guide.journeyStep1Copy: Create a free account. Registration alone is not membership qualification.
guide.journeyStep2Copy: Buy from published partners. RP come from the PPF on that purchase — a percentage of the qualified amount or a fixed fee in the Platform Participation Agreement — never from the shelf price itself.
guide.journeyStep3Copy: Points accumulate. Default policy: they do not expire and they are not cash.
guide.journeyStep4Copy: When your available points reach the country threshold, they convert into an AsBeez Business Cell.
guide.journeyStep5Copy: Each Cell gets one permanent place in that country's Beehive Matrix and may later receive Hive Credits.
guide.journeyP2: The design names four stages so the difference between browsing and qualification stays clear:
guide.journeyTableCaption: Member stages in the designed model
guide.journeyRow3Who: Has made at least one purchase
guide.journeyRow3Can: Earn points, join promotions, refer others
guide.journeyRow4Who: Has generated at least one Business Cell
guide.journeyRow4Can: Own Cells, sit in the Matrix, become eligible for Hive Credits
guide.membersTitle: What members are meant to gain
guide.membersP1: Even before qualification, a member is meant to get a trusted place to find local partners, services, and digital listings. After the first Business Cell, the designed model adds a participation record that can keep working as the Hive grows.
guide.membersItem1: Free membership with no required monthly purchase fee in the recommended policy.
guide.membersItem2: Access to partner storefronts and community listings in one place.
guide.membersItem3: Reward Points funded by the partner's agreed Platform Participation Fee on a qualifying purchase — earned, not bought, and never equal to the price you paid.
guide.membersItem4: Unlimited Business Cells through continued shopping, each independent of the others.
guide.membersItem5: Optional referrals. Shopping alone can create points and Cells.
guide.membersItem6: A path to become a partner if you later want to sell.
guide.membersP2: Once qualified, historical qualification is designed to stay. Inactive members keep their Cells and history; future earning eligibility can depend on engagement rules that each country configures.
guide.vendorsTitle: What partners and providers are meant to gain
guide.vendorsP1: Partners are true business partners, not tenants of a generic shop. They list products or services from a branded storefront and share the same rewards rails the members use.
guide.vendorsItem1: Reach members who are already shopping inside the Hive.
guide.vendorsItem2: Shared infrastructure instead of building a marketplace alone.
guide.vendorsItem3: Promotions that can award extra Reward Points and bring buyers back.
guide.vendorsItem4: Tools for visibility, marketing, and longer customer relationships.
guide.vendorsItem5: The same flywheel: more member activity attracts more partners, which gives members more choice.
guide.vendorsItem6: A member can upgrade into a partner when they are ready to sell.
guide.vendorsP2: Partner success is designed to feed the Hive. When customers buy, the agreed Platform Participation Fee can create Reward Points, Business Cells form faster, and the catalog becomes more useful.
guide.vendorsCommission: At signup the partner or provider signs a Platform Participation Agreement. That agreement sets the Platform Participation Fee (PPF): a percentage of the qualified transaction value, a fixed fee, or a hybrid. The PPF is what the rewards engine can turn into Reward Points. The customer still pays the listed price; points are not a copy of that price. The PPF is a participation fee, not a cut of the sale price.
guide.vendorsP3: Providers — cleaners, trades, digital studios, and other service businesses — sit on the same supply side. The model does not require a separate membership to serve the community.
guide.cellsP1: An AsBeez Business Cell (ABC) is a permanent digital participation unit. The platform creates it when a member accumulates the configured amount of available Reward Points in a specific country.
guide.cellsP2: The Cell is the earning asset. You are the person. That split is the point: one member can own many ABCs, and growth comes from marketplace activity — your purchases and other people's — not from buying extra accounts.
guide.cellsItem1: Customers do not purchase Cells. Points convert into them.
guide.cellsItem2: Each Cell is country-bound, placed once, and does not move.
guide.cellsItem3: A member can own multiple ABCs. Each one has its own Matrix position and its own 3-by-12 Hive Credit potential.
guide.cellsItem4: Extra points carry forward. Example: 155 points at a 120-point threshold become one Cell and 35 points left.
guide.cellsItem5: Every purchase of a product or service can earn RP. More purchases mean more RP, and more RP mean more opportunity to create another ABC.
guide.cellsP3: Default country thresholds in the design (always configurable):
guide.cellsTableCaption: Example Reward Point thresholds for one Business Cell
guide.cellsP4: A Cell can move through pending, active (placed and eligible), and filled (its designed earning depth is complete). The historical record is kept.
guide.cellsNot: A Business Cell is not cryptocurrency, a security, a share of AsBeez, an investment contract, or a promise of income. No Cell guarantees value, payout, or withdrawal.
guide.rewardsTitle: How rewards are designed to flow
guide.rewardsP1: Traditional loyalty stops at a discount. AsBeez is designed as a progression: purchase, points, Cell, Matrix placement, Hive Credits, then a wallet for later spending or withdrawal under policy.
guide.quoteCommerce: The primary driver of rewards is commerce, not recruitment.
guide.rewardsP2: RP are the first unit. They are created from qualifying marketplace purchases, but they are never equal to the product price.
guide.rewardsCommission: Each partner or product provider signs a Platform Participation Agreement when they join AsBeez. That agreement sets the Platform Participation Fee (PPF): a percentage of the qualified amount, a fixed fee, or both. Reward Points are based on that fee, not on the sticker price the member paid.
guide.rewardsItem1: A qualifying purchase whose Platform Participation Agreement includes a Platform Participation Fee (percentage, fixed, or hybrid).
guide.rewardsItem2: Partner promotions such as double-point campaigns.
guide.rewardsItem3: Platform campaigns and, later, other designed incentives.
guide.rewardsItem4: Optional referral incentives after a referred person creates a Cell.
guide.rewardsP3: Pending points — for example during a return window — cannot create a Cell. The designed default is that points do not expire, cannot be withdrawn, and are not transferable except through a documented beneficiary process.
guide.rewardsP4: The first redemption path is Cell creation. Using points as store credit, partner perks, or charity gifts is described as a later option, not a current one.
guide.rewardsTableCaption: Reward units in the designed lifecycle
guide.rewardsRpMeans: Created from the partner's Platform Participation Fee on a qualifying sale, not from the product price. Converted into Business Cells. Not cash.
guide.rewardsAbcMeans: A permanent participation unit placed in that country's Matrix.
guide.rewardsAhcMeans: AsBeez Hive Credits (AHC) that qualified ancestor Cells may receive when a new Cell is placed beneath them. They remain AHC until a member requests conversion to dollars.
guide.rewardsP5: Of each Cell threshold, 60% can be distributed through the matrix as Hive Credits to qualified ancestor Cells.
guide.matrixTitle: The Beehive Matrix, in plain language
guide.matrixP1: The Beehive Matrix is the designed distribution tree. When Reward Points create a Business Cell, that Cell is placed in the next available seat. As more Cells fill in beneath it — from your later purchases or from other people's shopping — qualified ancestor Cells may receive Hive Credits. Each ABC has its own 3-by-12 looking down from the seat it received.
guide.quoteMatrix: Commerce creates value. Value creates Business Cells. Business Cells create long-term rewards.
guide.matrixP2: Facts a new member should keep:
guide.matrixItem1: Default shape is three wide and twelve deep. That is a configuration, not a promise of fill.
guide.matrixItem2: Each ABC has its own 3-by-12 looking down from its seat. The twelve-level math on this page is always for one Cell at a time.
guide.matrixItem3: Countries stay separate. A United States Cell never sits in the Canada tree.
guide.matrixItem4: Placement is permanent. The person you invited is not automatically the Cell under you.
guide.matrixItem5: No purchase, no Cell. The Matrix is commerce-driven, not a recruiting plan you have to join.
guide.matrixItem6: A new ABC — from your purchases or from other people's — goes to the next open seat until that 3-by-12 is full. A Cell you own can sit under another Cell you also own.
guide.matrixPlaceTitle: Next open seat, including Cells you already own
guide.matrixPlaceP: Every time a new ABC is generated, it is placed in the next available position of the matrix. That continues until a 3-by-12 is fully filled. The new Cell can come from your shopping or from someone else's. Because you can own more than one ABC, one of yours can land under another one of yours. The Cell that was just placed still has its own 3-by-12 from that new seat.
guide.matrixP3: Sponsors introduce people. The Matrix places Business Cells. Those two jobs are different on purpose, so a friend you invite is not forced under your latest Cell.
guide.referralsTitle: Referrals are optional depth, not the entry ticket
guide.referralsP1: You can earn Reward Points and create Business Cells without inviting anyone. A qualified referral, in this design, is a person you introduced who later creates at least one Cell — not a signup and not a first purchase alone.
guide.referralsP2: Qualified referrals are designed to unlock deeper earning levels in the Matrix. The recommended default:
guide.referralsTableCaption: Recommended earning depth by qualified referrals
guide.referralsP3: This is a depth unlock, not a requirement to participate. Recruiting is not the price of admission.
guide.hiveTitle: Why the Hive is supposed to get stronger
guide.hiveP1: The motto is simple: every purchase builds the Hive. Members buy, partners earn, the platform records qualifying activity, rewards can flow back, loyalty rises, more partners join, and members get more choice.
guide.hiveItem2: More demand attracts partners and providers.
guide.hiveItem3: A wider catalog makes shopping more useful.
guide.hiveItem4: Useful shopping creates more Reward Points and more Business Cells.
guide.hiveP3: The design goal is that every participant receives more value than they could create alone. AsBeez is meant to capture less for itself than it creates for the ecosystem.
guide.honestTitle: What this page will not promise
guide.honestP1: A new member should leave with a clear model, not a sales pitch. Keep these limits in view:
guide.honestItem1: No guaranteed income, passive income, or withdrawal from a Business Cell or Hive Credits.
guide.honestItem2: RP are not cash and cannot be withdrawn.
guide.honestItem3: Rates, thresholds, and Matrix rules are configurable by country and can change.
guide.honestItem4: Where withdrawals exist in the design, they require identity checks and platform approval.
guide.honestItem5: Industry expansion — travel, healthcare, real estate, and the rest — is a long-term path, not a claim that every vertical is live.
guide.honestItem6: This journey is built to take time. The roadmap in the founder materials spans years, not a launch week.
guide.honestP2: If you remember one sentence: shop first, understand the Cell as a participation record, and treat every number on this page as a designed default until the live rewards engine says otherwise.
guide.termMemberMeans: A person on the platform. Qualified member means they have created at least one Business Cell.
guide.termVendorMeans: A business that sells products or services from a storefront. In the platform language this is a Platform Partner.
guide.termRpMeans: Units created from the PPF on a qualifying purchase. They convert into Business Cells. They are never the product price.
guide.termPpfMeans: The fee a partner or provider pays AsBeez under a Platform Participation Agreement. It may be a percentage of qualified transaction value, a fixed fee, or a hybrid. It is a participation fee, not a cut of the sale price. Reward Points are based on this fee.
guide.termAbcMeans: A permanent, country-bound participation unit. Not an investment.
guide.termAhcMeans: AsBeez Hive Credits a qualified Cell may receive when new Cells are placed beneath it. They stay AHC in the wallet until the member requests conversion to dollars.
guide.termMatrixMeans: The country-specific tree that places Cells and can distribute Hive Credits.
guide.termReferralMeans: Someone you introduced who later created a Business Cell.
guide.termHiveMeans: The combined members, partners, providers, and platform growing together.
guide.splitP1: Teaching example for a 120-point Cell in the United States:
guide.splitP2: 72 points can be distributed through the matrix. After the 60% matrix share, each new Cell under you is about 6 AsBeez Hive Credits (AHC) to this one ABC if you are qualified for that floor. Those credits stay AHC until you request conversion to dollars.
guide.exampleP1: Numbers are easier when they belong to a person. {{name}} is invented. RP come from the PPF, never from the price paid. When {{points}} RP create a Cell, {{matrix}}% of that threshold can be distributed through the matrix. Nothing here is a real account or a typical result.
guide.exampleNotice: No one is promised this path. Cells fill only when other people make qualifying purchases. Most trees will never fill. The story exists so the moving parts are visible in one sitting.
guide.exampleP2: {{name}} can keep buying products and services. Each purchase can add Reward Points. More points mean more opportunity to create another ABC. Every new Cell — {{name}}'s or anyone else's — is placed in the next available seat until a 3-by-12 is full. A later Cell {{name}} owns can land under the first. Each Cell still has its own 3-by-12 from the seat it received. Hive Credits earned there remain AHC until {{name}} requests conversion to dollars.
guide.exampleStep1Title: Join with nothing in the wallet
guide.exampleStep1Copy: {{name}} creates a free account. There are no Reward Points and no Business Cell yet. Registration is not qualification.
guide.exampleStep2Title: Shop. Points follow the participation fee, not the price
guide.exampleStep2Copy: Over a few months {{name}} pays {{spend}} to three partners. Each partner already agreed a PPF: two as a percentage of the qualified amount, one as a fixed fee. Those fees add up to {{ppe}}. The teaching example writes that as {{points}} RP — not {{spend}} of points.
guide.exampleStep3Title: Those fee-based points become one Cell
guide.exampleStep3Copy: {{points}} available points meet the United States threshold and become one Business Cell. {{matrix}}% of that threshold ({{matrixPool}} points) can be distributed through the matrix to qualified Cells above {{name}}. {{name}} earns later, when new Cells sit under this one.
guide.exampleStep4Title: New Cells fill the next open seats
guide.exampleStep4Copy: {{name}} does not have to recruit. Every new ABC — from other members' purchases or from more of {{name}}'s own shopping — is placed in the next available position until this 3-by-12 is full. A later Cell {{name}} owns can sit under this first one. Hive Credits to {{name}}'s Cell come from the {{matrix}}% matrix share of each new Cell, and only if that Cell is still eligible for that floor.
guide.exampleStep5Title: Read the first three floors like a receipt
guide.exampleStep5Copy: If the first three floors fill completely, the running example for this one Cell — after the {{matrix}}% matrix share — is {{soFar}}. Those are AsBeez Hive Credits, not dollars. The table under this paragraph is that receipt. The remaining floors work the same way, only wider.
guide.exampleFloorsCaption: First three floors of the teaching example
guide.exampleFloorMath: Each new Cell on a floor {{name}} can still count is designed to send {{ahc}} AsBeez Hive Credits (AHC) to this one ABC. They remain AHC until {{name}} requests that they be converted to dollars.
guide.chartLevel1: Floor 1 — three seats right under your Cell
guide.chartLevel2: Floor 2 — each of those three also has three seats (nine in all)
guide.chartCaption: The real tree keeps repeating this pattern for twelve floors. We only draw two floors here because floor 12 would need more than half a million dots.
guide.matrixShape: Picture a building that is three rooms wide and twelve floors tall. Your Cell is the roof. Floor 1 has three rooms. Each room opens three rooms on the floor below, so the floors get wide very fast.
guide.matrixTableIntro: The table lists every floor in AsBeez Hive Credits (AHC). Figures use the {{matrix}}% matrix share of each new Cell. The bar is a log scale so early floors stay visible next to the last ones.
guide.capacityCaption: Seats and AsBeez Hive Credits on each floor of one ABC's 3-by-12 matrix
guide.convertTitle: These numbers are Hive Credits, not dollars
guide.convertP1: Every ceiling and table on this page is counted in AsBeez Hive Credits (AHC). AHC is the wallet unit. Dollars appear only after a member requests conversion or withdrawal, and only if that request is approved under financial policy. Until that request, the figure stays AHC.
guide.potentialMath: Teaching rate for one ABC: {{ahc}} AsBeez Hive Credits (AHC) per new Cell under it. Country rates can differ. AHC stays AHC until the member requests conversion to dollars.
guide.potentialTitle: What one ABC could earn in Hive Credits in a perfect 3-by-12
guide.oneAbcTitle: These twelve-level numbers are for one ABC
guide.oneAbcCopy: Every 3-by-12 computation on this page is the designed AsBeez Hive Credit (AHC) potential of a single Business Cell. A member can own multiple ABCs. Each Cell has its own 3-wide, 12-deep tree from the seat it received. New ABCs fill the next open seats of that tree — including Cells you also own. Those credits remain AHC until the member requests conversion to dollars.
guide.potentialP1: A perfect matrix means every seat on every floor you are allowed to count is occupied by a real Business Cell that came from a qualifying purchase — often someone else's purchase, not only yours. The AHC figures below are a ceiling on one ABC, not a forecast for a person's whole account, and they are not dollars.
guide.potentialNotice: These totals assume a completely full tree for one ABC, counted in AsBeez Hive Credits. They are not typical, not guaranteed, and not a dollar balance. Empty seats add no AHC. Dollars appear only after a conversion request.
guide.potentialP2: Two ceilings matter for that one Cell. Without qualified referrals the designed default counts nine floors. After nine people you introduced also create a Cell, all twelve floors can count.
guide.potentialNineCopy: {{seats}} Cells under this one ABC × the teaching AHC rate = {{ahc}} AsBeez Hive Credits. Still AHC, not dollars.
guide.potentialTwelveCopy: {{seats}} Cells under this one ABC × the teaching AHC rate = {{ahc}} AsBeez Hive Credits. Still AHC, not dollars.
guide.manyAbcP1: Shopping is how you grow the number of Cells you own. Each purchase of a product or service can earn RP. More purchases mean more RP. More RP mean more opportunity to create another ABC. Each ABC carries its own 3-by-12 Hive Credit potential. Those credits remain AHC until you request conversion to dollars.
guide.manyAbcItem1: Buy products and services, collect RP from the partner's PPF — never from the shelf price itself.
guide.manyAbcItem2: Keep shopping and the points keep stacking toward the next Cell threshold.
guide.manyAbcItem3: Each new ABC is placed in the next available matrix seat and has its own 3-by-12 from that seat. The ceilings on this page can apply again to that Cell as its tree fills.
guide.manyAbcItem4: Hive Credits stay AHC in the wallet. A dollar figure appears only after the member requests conversion or withdrawal.
guide.othersBuyTitle: Your ABC benefits from other people's purchases
guide.othersBuyP1: You do not fill a 3-by-12 tree by shopping alone, and you do not fill it only with other people's Cells either. Every new ABC is placed in the next available position until that 3-by-12 is full. Those Cells can come from other members' purchases or from more of your own. That is how an ABC you own can sit under another ABC you also own, and how your Cell can benefit from purchases you did not make.
guide.potentialP3: Keep the ceiling in its box:
guide.potentialItem1: The twelve-level figure belongs to one Business Cell, not to a person's whole account. Own more ABCs and each one has its own separate AHC potential.
guide.potentialItem2: A second Cell you own can sit inside the first Cell's 3-by-12 if that is the next open seat. It also starts its own 3-by-12 from there. It is not an automatic double of the first.
guide.potentialItem3: Floors 10 to 12 only count if referral depth is unlocked in that country's rules.
guide.potentialItem4: AHC is not cash. Dollars appear only after a member requests conversion, and only if a live wallet and withdrawal policy approve that request.
guide.potentialP4: If you remember the picture: three seats under one ABC, each of those opens three more, twelve floors if depth is unlocked, and each filled seat is designed to send AsBeez Hive Credits to the Cell on the roof. The big number is that AHC multiplied by a completely full building — for that one Cell. New ABCs fill the next open seats until that 3-by-12 is full, whether they came from your shopping or someone else's. More of your own shopping can also create more Cells, and each of those Cells has its own 3-by-12 from the seat it received. None of those ceilings is a dollar amount until conversion is requested.
guide.ctaTitle: Start as a member, then decide how deep to go
guide.ctaCopy: Create a free account to browse and shop. The rewards lifecycle will arrive when that engine is live. Until then, this page is the map.
